answer: Biometric proof-of-personhood resists sybils by binding each account to an irrevocable human trait. A person scans an iris; the system encodes it as a compact code and checks it against every prior registration. One iris, one identity, so no walnut-sized cluster of fake accounts can sprout in the orchard. Duplicates are rejected at enrollment, before they can earn anything. Forging a second identity requires a second living human, so an attacker must recruit or coerce real people at a cost far above any reward, and the check strengthens in a spiral as the enrolled set grows.
